parameters.name: phSimConnect
parameters.type: Pointer to a handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: szName
parameters.type: Pointer to a null-terminated string containing an appropriate name for the client program.

parameters.name: hWnd
parameters.type: Handle to a Windows object. Set this to NULL if the handle is not being used. UserEventWin32

parameters.name: UserEventWin32
parameters.type: Code number that the client can specify. Set this to 0 if it is not being used.

parameters.name: hEventHandle
parameters.type: A Windows Event handle. A client can be written to respond to Windows Events, rather than use a polling and callback system, which can be a more efficient process if the client does not have to respond very frequently to changes in data in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020.

parameters.name: ConfigIndex
parameters.type: The configuration index. The SimConnect.cfg file can contain a number of configurations, identified in sections with the [SimConnect] or [SimConnect.N] titles. Setting this configuration index indicates which configuration settings to use for this SimConnect client. This is useful for applications that communicate with a number of different machines that are running Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020. The default configuration index is zero (matching a [SimConnect] entry in a SimConnect.cfg file). Note the E_INVALIDARG return value.

functions.name: SimConnect_MapClientEventToSimEvent
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_MapClientEventToSimEvent( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_EVENT_ID EventID, const char* EventName );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: EventID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client event.

parameters.name: EventName
parameters.type: Specifies the Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 event name. Refer to the Event IDs document for a list of event names (listed under String Name). If the event name includes one or more periods (such as "Custom.Event" in the example below) then they are custom events specified by the client, and will only be recognized by another client (and not Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020) that has been coded to receive such events. No Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 events include periods. If no entry is made for this parameter, the event is private to the client. Alternatively enter a decimal number in the format "#nnnn" or a hex number in the format "#0xnnnn", where these numbers are in the range THIRD_PARTY_EVENT_ID_MIN and THIRD_PARTY_EVENT_ID_MAX, in order to receive events from third-party add-ons to Flight Simulator X.

functions.name: SimConnect_TransmitClientEvent
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_TransmitClientEvent( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID ObjectID, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_EVENT_ID EventID, DWORD dwData, SIMCONNECT_NOTIFICATION_GROUP_ID GroupID, SIMCONNECT_EVENT_FLAG Flags );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the server defined object. If this parameter is set to SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID_USER, then the transmitted event will be sent to the other clients in priority order. If this parameters contains another object ID, then the event will be sent direct to that sim-object, and no other clients will receive it.

parameters.name: EventID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client event.

parameters.name: dwData
parameters.type: Double word containing any additional number required by the event. This is often zero. If the event is a Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 event, then refer to the Event IDs document for information on this additional value. If the event is a custom event, then any value put in this parameter will be available to the clients that receive the event.

parameters.name: GroupID
parameters.type: The default behavior is that this specifies the GroupID of the event. The SimConnect server will use the priority of this group to send the message to all clients with a lower priority. To receive the event notification other SimConnect clients must have subscribed to receive the event. See the explanation of SimConnect Priorities. The exception to the default behavior is set by the SIMCONNECT_EVENT_FLAG_GROUPID_IS_PRIORITY flag, described below.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.type: One or more of the flags shown in the table below.

parameters.name: EventID

parameters.name: GroupID
parameters.type: The default behavior is that this specifies the GroupID of the event. The SimConnect server will use the priority of this group to send the message to all clients with a lower priority. To receive the event notification other SimConnect clients must have subscribed to receive the event. See the explanation of SimConnect Priorities. The exception to the default behavior is set by the SIMCONNECT_EVENT_FLAG_GROUPID_IS_PRIORITY flag, described below.

parameters.name: Flags

If the event is a custom event, then any values put in these parameters will be available to the clients that receive the event.

functions.name: SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObject
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObject( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_DATA_REQUEST_ID RequestID, SIMCONNECT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID ObjectID, SIMCONNECT_PERIOD Period, SIMCONNECT_DATA_REQUEST_FLAG Flags = 0, DWORD origin = 0, DWORD interval = 0, DWORD limit = 0 );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: RequestID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined group.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined data definition.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 object that the data should be about. This ID can be SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID_USER (to specify the user's aircraft) or obtained from a SIMCONNECT_RECV_SIMOBJECT_DATA_BYTYPE structure after a call to SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObjectType. Also refer to the note on developing clients for multiplayer mode in the Remarks section below.

parameters.name: Period
parameters.type: One member of the SIMCONNECT_PERIOD enumeration type, specifying how often the data is to be sent by the server and received by the client.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.type: A DWORD containing one or more of the values shown in the table below this one.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.type: The number of Period events that should elapse before transmission of the data begins. The default is zero, which means transmissions will start immediately.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.type: The number of Period events that should elapse between transmissions of the data. The default is zero, which means the data is transmitted every Period.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.type: The number of times the data should be transmitted before this communication is ended. The default is zero, which means the data should be transmitted endlessly.

functions.name: SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObjectType
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObjectType( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_DATA_REQUEST_ID RequestID, SIMCONNECT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, DWORD dwRadiusMeters, SIMCONNECT_SIMOBJECT_TYPE type );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: RequestID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined request. This is used later by the client to identify which data has been received. This value should be unique for each request, re-using a RequestID will overwrite any previous request using the same ID.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined data definition.

parameters.name: dwRadiusMeters
parameters.type: Double word containing the radius in meters. If this is set to zero only information on the user aircraft will be returned, although this value is ignored if type is set to SIMCONNECT_SIMOBJECT_TYPE_USER. The error SIMCONNECT_EXCEPTION_OUT_OF_BOUNDS will be returned if a radius is given and it exceeds the maximum allowed (200,000 meters, or 200 Km).

parameters.name: type
parameters.type: Specifies the type of object to receive information on. One member of the SIMCONNECT_SIMOBJECT_TYPE enumeration type

functions.name: SimConnect_AddToDataDefinition
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_AddToDataDefinition( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, const char* DatumName, const char* UnitsName, SIMCONNECT_DATATYPE DatumType = SIMCONNECT_DATATYPE_FLOAT64, float fEpsilon = 0, DWORD DatumID = SIMCONNECT_UNUSED );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined data definition.

parameters.name: DatumName
parameters.type: Specifies the name of the Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 simulation variable. See the Simulation Variables documents for tables of variable names. If an index is required then it should be appended to the variable name following a colon, see the example for DEFINITION_2 below. Indexes are numbered from 1 (not zero). Simulation variable names are not case-sensitive (so can be entered in upper or lower case).

parameters.name: UnitsName
parameters.type: Specifies the units of the variable. See Simulation Variable Units for tables of acceptable unit names. It is possible to specify different units to receive the data in, from those specified in the Simulation Variables document. The alternative units must come under the same heading (such as Angular Velocity, or Volume, as specified in the Units of Measurement section of the Simulation Variables document). For strings and structures enter "NULL" for this parameter.

parameters.name: DatumType
parameters.type: One member of the SIMCONNECT_DATATYPE enumeration type. This parameter is used to determine what datatype should be used to return the data. The default is SIMCONNECT_DATATYPE_FLOAT64. Note that the structure data types are legitimate parameters here.

parameters.name: fEpsilon
parameters.type: If data is requested only when it changes (see the flags parameter of SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObject) a change will only be reported if it is greater than the value of this parameter (not greater than or equal to). The default is zero, so even the tiniest change will initiate the transmission of data. Set this value appropriately so insignificant changes are not transmitted. This can be used with integer data, the floating point fEpsilon value is first truncated to its integer component before the comparison is made (for example, an fEpsilon value of 2.9 truncates to 2, so a data change of 2 will not trigger a transmission, and a change of 3 will do so).

parameters.name: DatumID
parameters.type: Specifies a client defined datum ID. The default is zero. Use this to identify the data received if the data is being returned in tagged format (see the flags parameter of SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObject. There is no need to specify datum IDs if the data is not being returned in tagged format.

functions.name: SimConnect_SetDataOnSimObject
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_SetDataOnSimObject( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID ObjectID, SIMCONNECT_DATA_SET_FLAG Flags, DWORD ArrayCount, DWORD cbUnitSize, void* pDataSet );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client defined data definition.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the Microsoft Flight Simulator object that the data should be about. This ID can be SIMCONNECT_OBJECT_ID_USER (to specify the user's aircraft) or obtained from a SIMCONNECT_RECV_SIMOBJECT_DATA_BYTYPE structure after a call to SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObjectType. Also refer to the note on "multiplayer mode" at the end of the remarks for SimConnect_RequestDataOnSimObject.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.type: Null, or one or more of the flags listed below.

parameters.name: ArrayCount
parameters.type: Specifies the number of elements in the data array. A count of zero is interpreted as one element. Ensure that the data array has been initialized completely before transmitting it to Microsoft Flight Simulator. Failure to properly initialize all array elements may result in unexpected behavior.

parameters.name: cbUnitSize
parameters.type: Specifies the size of each element in the data array in bytes.

parameters.name: pDataSet
parameters.type: Pointer to the data that is to be written. If the data is not in tagged format, this should point to the block of data. If the data is in tagged format this should point to the first tag name (datumID), which is always four bytes long, which should be followed by the data itself. Any number of tag name/value pairs can be specified this way, the server will use the cbUnitSize parameter to determine how much data has been sent.

parameters.type: A unique ID for the client data area, specified by the client. If the ID number is already in use, an error will be returned.

functions.name: SimConnect_AddToClientDataDefinition
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_AddToClientDataDefinition( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, DWORD dwOffset, DWORD dwSizeOrType, float fEpsilon = 0, DWORD DatumID = SIMCONNECT_UNUSED );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client-defined client data definition.

parameters.name: dwOffset
parameters.type: Double word containing the offset into the client area, where the new addition is to start. Set this to SIMCONNECT_CLIENTDATAOFFSET_AUTO for the offsets to be calculated by the SimConnect server.

parameters.name: dwSizeOrType
parameters.type: Double word containing either the size of the client data in bytes, or one of the constant values defined in the table below (note that these definitions have a negative value, all positive values will be treated as a size parameter).

parameters.name: fEpsilon
parameters.type: If data is requested only when it changes (see the flags parameter of SimConnect_RequestClientData, a change will only be reported if it is greater than the value of this parameter (not greater than or equal to). The default is zero, so even the tiniest change will initiate the transmission of data. Set this value appropriately so insignificant changes are not transmitted. This can be used with integer data, the floating point fEpsilon value is first truncated to its integer component before the comparison is made (for example, an fEpsilon value of 2.9 truncates to 2, so a data change of 2 will not trigger a transmission, and a change of 3 will do so). This parameter only applies if one of the six constant values listed above has been set in the dwSizeOrType parameter, if a size has been specified SimConnect has no record of the type of data being sent, so cannot do a meaningful comparison of values.

parameters.name: DatumID
parameters.type: Specifies a client defined datum ID. The default is zero. Use this to identify the data received if the data is being returned in tagged format (see the flags parameter of SimConnect_RequestClientData. There is no need to specify datum IDs if the data is not being returned in tagged format.

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: ClientDataID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client data area. Before calling this function for the first time on one client area, call SimConnect_MapClientDataNameToID to map an ID to the unique client data area name. This name must match the name specified by the client creating the data area with the SimConnect_MapClientDataNameToID and SimConnect_CreateClientData functions.

parameters.name: RequestID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client-defined request. This is used later by the client to identify which data has been received. This value should be unique for each request, re-using a RequestID will overwrite any previous request using the same ID.

parameters.name: DefineID
parameters.type: Specifies the ID of the client-defined data definition. This definition specifies the data that should be sent to the client.

parameters.name: Period
parameters.type: One member of the SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_DATA_PERIOD enumeration type, specifying how often the data is to be sent by the server and received by the client.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.type: A DWORD containing one or more of the values from the table below.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.type: The number of Period events that should elapse before transmission of the data begins. The default is zero, which means transmissions will start immediately.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.type: The number of Period events that should elapse between transmissions of the data. The default is zero, which means the data is transmitted every Period.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.type: The number of times the data should be transmitted before this communication is ended. The default is zero, which means the data should be transmitted endlessly.

functions.name: SimConnect_SetClientData
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_SetClientData( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_DATA_ID ClientDataID, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_DATA_DEFINITION_ID DefineID, DWORD Flags, DWORD dwReserved, DWORD cbUnitSize, void* pDataSet );

parameters.name: hSimConnect

parameters.name: ClientDataID

parameters.name: Flags

parameters.name: pDataSet
parameters.type: Pointer to the data that is to be written. If the data is not in tagged format, this should point to the block of client data. If the data is in tagged format this should point to the first tag name (datumID), which is always four bytes long, which should be followed by the data itself. Any number of tag name/value pairs can be specified this way, the server will use the cbUnitSize parameter to determine how much data has been sent.

functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_RequestReservedKey( HANDLE hSimConnect, SIMCONNECT_CLIENT_EVENT_ID EventID, const char* szKeyChoice1, const char* szKeyChoice2 = "", const char* szKeyChoice3 = "" );

parameters.name: hSimConnect

functions.name: SimConnect_RequestResponseTimes
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_RequestResponseTimes( HANDLE hSimConnect, DWORD nCount, float* fElapsedSeconds );

parameters.name: hSimConnect
parameters.type: Handle to a SimConnect object.

parameters.name: nCount
parameters.type: Integer containing the number of elements in the array of floats. This should be set to five for the full range of timings, but can be less if only the first few are of interest. There is no point creating an array of greater than five floats.

parameters.name: fElapsedSeconds
parameters.type: An array of nCount floats, containing the times. The five elements will contain the following: 0 - total round trip time 1 - time from the request till the packet is sent 2 - time from the request till the packet is received by the server 3 - time from the request till the response is made by the server 4 - time from the server response to the client receives the packet.

functions.name: SimConnect_InsertString
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_InsertString( char* pDest, DWORD cbDest, void** ppEnd, DWORD* pcbStringV, const char* pSource );

parameters.name: pDest
parameters.type: Pointer to where the source string is to be written in the destination object.

parameters.name: cbDest
parameters.type: The size of the remaining space in the destination object.

parameters.name: ppEnd
parameters.type: Pointer to a pointer, (usually a pointer to a char pointer). On return the pointer locates the end of the string in the structure, and hence the starting position for any other string to be included in the structure.

parameters.name: pcbStringV
parameters.type: Pointer to a DWORD. On returning this DWORD will contain the size of the source string in bytes.

parameters.name: pSource
parameters.type: Pointer to the source string.

functions.name: SimConnect_RetrieveString
functions.signature: HRESULT SimConnect_RetrieveString( SIMCONNECT_RECV* pData, DWORD cbData, void* pStringV, char** ppszString, DWORD* pcbString );

parameters.name: pData
parameters.type: Pointer to a SIMCONNECT_RECV structure, containing the data.

parameters.name: cbData
parameters.type: The size of the structure that inherits the SIMCONNECT_RECV structure, in bytes.

parameters.name: pStringV
parameters.type: Pointer to a the start of the variable length string within the structure.

parameters.name: ppszString
parameters.type: Specifies a pointer to a pointer to a character buffer that should be large enough to contain the maximum length of string that might be returned. On return this buffer should contain the retrieved string.

parameters.name: pcbString
parameters.type: Pointer to a DWORD. On return this contains the length of the string in bytes.
